# Adjudication Task — Chapter 266

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃266화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“껍질을 깼구나.”
  6|
  7|맑은 목소리가 울려 퍼졌다.
  8|
  9|청풍이 연화봉의 햇살과 푸른 하늘을 떠올린 데 비해, 혈주는 심장이 철렁 내려앉는 듯한 충격을 느꼈다.
 10|
 11|고작 이십여 장 밖의 기척을 감지하지 못했다. 다른 누구도 아닌 자신이.
 12|
 13|그는 오솔길을 걸어 올라오는 한 사람을 보며 눈매를 가늘게 떴다.
 14|
 15|‘저놈은…….’
 16|
 17|호리호리한 체구에 서글서글한 인상. 기껏해야 이십 대 중반으로 보이는 청년이다.
 18|
 19|검집도 없이 허리춤에 대충 찔러 넣은 검은 온통 붉게 녹이 슬어 있었다.
 20|
 21|혈주의 입술 사이로 메마른 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
 22|
 23|“상승검?”
 24|
 25|청년, 종리추가 빙긋 웃었다.
 26|
 27|“늘 걱정이었다.”
 28|
 29|“뭐?”
 30|
 31|“두려움을 모르는 천진난만한 아이가 무림에 나가면 얼마나 큰 파도를 겪을지.”
 32|
 33|“이게 무슨 개소리…….”
 34|
 35|말을 이으려던 혈주는 불현듯 깨달았다. 처음부터 종리추의 모든 말과 행동이 오직 한 사람에게로 향하고 있었음을.
 36|
 37|“하지만 이제 되었다. 정말 잘 이겨 내 주었어.”
 38|
 39|따스한 시선과 목소리.
 40|
 41|이윽고 힘겹게 헐떡이던 청풍의 입가에 희미한 미소가 맺혔다.
 42|
 43|그 모습을 지켜본 혈주는 헛웃음을 흘렸다.
 44|
 45|“이것들 봐라…….”
 46|
 47|이건 숫제 없는 사람 취급이 아닌가. 천(天) 내부에서도 수많은 이들의 두려움과 경외를 받는 그를 두고 말이다.
 48|
 49|하룻강아지 같은 놈들의 노골적인 무시에 저절로 손아귀에 힘이 들어갔다.
 50|
 51|우득.
 52|
 53|“커헉!”
 54|
 55|뼈 어긋나는 소리와 함께 청풍의 입술 사이로 핏물이 울컥 터져 나왔다.
 56|
 57|고통 어린 신음을 흘린 청풍이 혼절함과 동시에, 종리추의 조용한 목소리가 혈주의 귓가를 울렸다.
 58|
 59|“그만하시게.”
 60|
 61|웃음이 사라진 종리추의 얼굴을 보자 기분이 한결 나아졌다.
 62|
 63|혈주가 씩 웃으며 입을 열었다.
 64|
 65|“이제야 내가 보이는 모양이군.”
 66|
 67|“진즉에 보고 있었네. 멀어지는 뒷모습만 쫓다가 놓쳐 버렸지만.”
 68|
 69|가만 듣던 혈주가 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
 70|
 71|“네놈이었나? 나를 방해했던 그 겁 없는 놈이.”
 72|
 73|“한발 늦었지. 안타까운 일이야.”
 74|
 75|침착하게 대답하는 종리추를, 혈주가 천천히 위아래로 훑었다.
 76|
 77|‘상승검 종리추. 이놈이 바로 그놈이라고?’
 78|
 79|놈이 끼어든 것은 법왕 굉도의 숨통을 끊어 놓으려던 찰나였다. 급속하게 가까워지는 기척에 결국 끝장을 보지 못하고 돌아서야 했다.
 80|
 81|‘그때 느낀 바로는 최소 십왕(十王)을 뛰어넘는 기세였다.’
 82|
 83|아무리 혈주라도 무림맹 내부에서 발목이 묶인다면 낭패를 겪을 수밖에 없다. 그가 죽어 가는 굉도를 두고 몸을 뺀 후에도 놈은 한참을 더 추격해 왔다.
 84|
 85|‘하마터면 따라잡힐 뻔했지.’
 86|
 87|다행히도 혈주가 익힌 무공은 상리(常理)를 아득히 벗어난 것이었다.
 88|
 89|그런데 그 정체불명의 고수가 바로 종리추일 줄이야. 혈주는 의심 가득한 눈빛을 쏘아 보냈다.
 90|
 91|“벌써 여기까지 쫓아오다니. 발이 빠르군.”
 92|
 93|“자네만큼은 아닐세. 듣도 보도 못한 경신법을 쓰던데.”
 94|
 95|혈주의 눈매가 가늘어졌다.
 96|
 97|상대는 새파랗게 어린놈이다. 청풍과의 친분도 두터워 보였고, 무공의 경지는 도무지 믿기지 않을 만큼 뛰어나다.
 98|
 99|“네놈, 무신(武神)과는 어떤 관계냐?”
100|
101|종리추가 습관처럼 매끈한 턱을 쓰다듬었다.
102|
103|“무신이라……. 몇 가지 가르침을 받긴 했지.”
104|
105|“제자인가?”
106|
107|“젖먹이 어린아이에게도 배울 점은 있다네. 살면서 스쳐 가는 모두가 서로에게 스승이고 제자야.”
108|
109|“뜬구름 잡는 선문답은 집어치워. 당장 이놈의 목을 꺾어 버리기 전에.”
110|
111|그러나 대답 대신 돌아온 것은 종리추의 차분한 눈빛이었다.
112|
113|보고 있자면 한없이 빨려 들어갈 것처럼 깊었고, 한편으로는 바람 불지 않는 날의 호수처럼 잔잔했다.
114|
115|‘뭐지, 이 기분은?’
116|
117|이상한 일이다. 단지 눈을 마주했을 뿐인데 쉽사리 손아귀에 힘이 들어가지 않는다.
118|
119|아니, 오히려 힘이 스르륵 빠져나가는 느낌이다. 보이지 않는 뭔가가 손목을 잡고 놓아 주지 않는 것처럼.
120|
121|‘이건 마치…….’
122|
123|문득 뒤를 잇는 생각에 혈주는 이를 악물었다.
124|
125|아니다.
126|
127|그건 있을 수 없는 일이다. 이런 정파의 떨거지를 보고 감히 ‘그분’을 떠올리다니.
128|
129|‘그럴 리 없어. 저런 놈 따위, 단숨에 베어 버리면 그만이다.’
130|
131|억지로 마음을 다잡았다. 하지만 마음속에서는 정체 모를 불안감이 피어오르고 있었다.
132|
133|과연 저놈을 이길 수 있을까, 이 자리를 벗어날 수 있을까 하는 의문이었다.
134|
135|혈주는 바짝 마른 입술을 느리게 핥았다.
136|
137|“네놈……. 도대체 정체가 뭐냐?”
138|
139|천하 곳곳에 펼쳐진 암천의 정보망은 넓고도 촘촘하다. 그러나 단 한 사람, 종리추의 정체만은 밝혀 내지 못했다.
140|
141|얼굴도, 출신도 짐작할 수 없는 미지의 인물.
142|
143|종리추가 고개를 갸웃거렸다.
144|
145|“그게 중요한가?”
146|
147|“뭐?”
148|
149|“말 몇 마디로 자네를 멈추게 할 수 있다면 대답해 줬겠지. 하지만 자네는 멈추지 않을 거야.”
150|
151|잔잔한 목소리가 이어졌다.
152|
153|“지금도 사경을 헤매는 이들이 있네. 스스로 멈추기 싫다면 멈춰 세우는 수밖에.”
154|
155|스르륵.
156|
157|말을 끝낸 종리추가 허리춤에 대충 찔러 넣은 검을 뽑아 들었다. 엉망진창 녹슨 검신이 드러나자 혈주의 입가에 비웃음이 서렸다.
158|
159|“나를 멈춰 세워? 검 같지도 않은 그따위 물건으로?”
160|
161|“글쎄, 아직 생각보다 쓸 만한 것 같네만.”
162|
163|“그 검으로 누굴 베어 본 적이나 있나?”
164|
165|“수도 없이 베었지. 별로 자랑스러운 기억은 아니야.”
166|
167|“나를 그런 어중이떠중이와 비교하면 곤란하지. 마지막으로 벤 것이 누구냐? 화전민이나 다를 바 없는 산적? 아니면…….”
168|
169|그 순간, 종리추의 입술 사이로 나지막한 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
170|
171|“천독마군(天毒魔君).”
172|
173|혈주의 몸이 덜컥 굳었다.
174|
175|천독마군.
176|
177|무림인이라면 모를 수 없는 별호다.
178|
179|정마대전 당시, 천마신교의 교주인 천마를 신으로 떠받들며 천하를 휩쓸던 대마두 중의 대마두가 아닌가.
180|
181|한때 천하의 절반을 집어삼킨 마교의 이인자. 그가 바로 천독마군이었다.
182|
183|그러나 그 역시 한낱 무림인의 운명을 벗어나지는 못했다.
184|
185|나날이 흉명을 더해 가던 어느 날, 한 사람과 맞닥트린 것이다. 그날 천독마군은 죽음을 맞이했고, 그를 죽인 자는 새로운 이름을 얻었다.
186|
187|“검성(劍星)……!”
188|
189|혈주의 몸이 번개에 관통당한 것처럼 파르르 떨렸다.
190|
191|검성 매종학.
192|
193|종리추의 정체를 짐작할 때 아주 잠깐 뇌리를 스쳐 간 이름이다. 그러나 이내 고개를 저었었다.
194|
195|있을 수 없는, 있어서도 안 되는 일이니까.
196|
197|간신히 쥐어짜 낸 목소리가 입 밖으로 흘러나왔다.
198|
199|“당신이…… 당신이 어떻게…….”
200|
201|종리추, 아니 검성 매종학이 검신을 쓰다듬으며 대답했다.
202|
203|“정마대전이 끝나자 문득 그런 생각이 들었지. 이제 무엇을 해야 하나? 고민은 길지 않았네. 그저 무공이 좋았거든.”
204|
205|사악. 사아악.
206|
207|손에 어린 자줏빛 수강(手罡)이 스칠 때마다 붉게 녹슨 검신이 투명한 본디 모습을 드러냈다.
208|
209|“끊임없이 무공에 매진했네. 뒤늦게 들인 손주 같은 아이가 내 제자였고, 때로는 내게 스승이 되어 주었지. 그렇게 대성(大成)을 이뤘다고 생각한 순간, 또 다른 벽이 보이더군.”
210|
211|검성 매종학.
212|
213|이미 수십 년 전 드높은 경지에 올라 있던 위대한 무인은 다시 한번 새로운 영역에 발을 디뎠다.
214|
215|이미 모든 면에서 준비되어 있던 그에게, 더 높은 깨달음이 찾아온 것이다.
216|
217|“반로환동(返老還童)까지는 나도 예상치 못했네. 어쨌든 생각지도 못하게 육신이 어려지니 바깥세상이 궁금해지더군. 일 년 전 뛰쳐나간 괘씸한 손주놈 생각도 나고 말이야.”
218|
219|그렇게 검성 매종학은 세상으로 나왔고, 종리추라는 이름으로 천하를 유람했다.
220|
221|그는 이미 까마득한 과거의 인물. 약관의 청년으로 돌아간 매종학을 의심하는 아무도 없었다.
222|
223|천하 곳곳에 그물을 뻗어 놓은 암천도 예외는 아니었다.
224|
225|“즐거운 시간이었네. 자네들이 나타나기 전까지는.”
226|
227|사아악!
228|
229|검신을 뒤덮었던 마지막 녹이 벗겨져 나갔다.
230|
231|마침내 본 모습을 되찾은 애검이 서늘한 빛을 뿌렸다.
232|
233|수백, 혹은 수천. 셀 수 없이 많은 마두의 피를 머금은 검이 혈주를 향해 겨누어진다.
234|
235|“이 검, 내 말대로 아직 쓸 만하지 않나?”
236|
237|다음 순간, 자줏빛 섬광이 뿜어졌다.
238|
239|서걱!
240|
241|“……어?”
242|
243|혈주는 눈을 깜빡였다.
244|
245|느려진 시간 속, 천천히 쓰러지는 청풍의 모습이 시야에 들어왔다.
246|
247|이미 혼절한 그의 목을 움켜잡은, 누군가의 낯익은 손목도.
248|
249|‘저건…….’
250|
251|내 손인데.
252|
253|이어져야 할 생각은, 솟구치는 핏물과 고통에 파묻혔다. 자신도 모르게 딱 벌어진 입에서 비명이 터져 나왔다.
254|
255|“크아악!”
256|
257|하지만 아직 끝난 것이 아니었다.
258|
259|비명과 함께 뒷걸음질 치는 그에게 서늘한 목소리가 따라붙었다.
260|
261|“씻을 수 없는 업을 쌓았으니 대가를 치러야 하지 않겠나.”
262|
263|쉬이익!
264|
265|혈주는 전신의 털이 곤두서는 듯했다.
266|
267|마치 환영 같은 광경이었다. 모든 풍경이 지워지고 오직 자신의 가슴을 향한 한 자루의 검만이 그의 모든 것을 사로잡았다.
268|
269|스르륵.
270|
271|허공을 유영하는 한 자루의 검. 자하신공의 자줏빛 강기가 서른여섯 송이의 매화로 화해 사방에 흩날렸다.
272|
273|그 아름다운 광경에 혈주는 신음처럼 중얼거렸다.
274|
275|“매화삼십육검.”
276|
277|그러나 다르다. 분명히 달랐다.
278|
279|앞서 청풍이 펼친 매화삼십육검이 절기(絶技)라면, 지금 매종학이 펼쳐 내는 것은 무공을 넘어선 신기(神技)였다.
280|
281|바로 그런 신기가 혈주의 전신 요혈을 파고들고 있었다.
282|
283|‘이건…… 막을 수 없다.’
284|
285|경악한 혈주가 황급히 몸을 날리려던 그 순간이었다.
286|
287|덥석!
288|
289|누군가의 손아귀가 그의 발목을 잡아챘다.
290|
291|이미 힘을 다하고 기절한 줄 알았던 진태경이 피에 젖은 이빨을 드러내며 웃고 있었다.
292|
293|“어딜 가. 이 씹새꺄.”
294|
295|“놈-!”
296|
297|파파파팟!
298|
299|말은 이어지지 못했다. 혈주의 눈동자에 자줏빛 섬광이 가득 찼다. 피가 튀고 살이 베였다. 엄청난 극통에 순간 뇌리가 하얗게 물들었다.
300|
301|“커헉!”
302|
303|차원이 달랐다. 십여 장의 거리를 지우며 달려드는 검기를 막을 방법은 어디에도 없었다.
304|

He was a figure from the distant past. No one suspected that the young man in his early twenties was Mae Jonghak.

[P116]
Not even Dark Heaven, whose web stretched across the land.

[P117]
“It was an enjoyable time. Until you people appeared.”

[P118]
Shhk!

[P119]
The last traces of rust peeled away.

[P120]
At last, his cherished sword regained its true form and gleamed coldly.

[P121]
Hundreds—perhaps thousands. The sword that had drunk the blood of countless fiends now pointed at the Blood Lord.

[P122]
“Just as I said, isn’t this sword still useful?”

[P123]
The next instant, a violet flash erupted.

[P124]
Slash!

[P125]
“…Huh?”

[P126]
The Blood Lord blinked.

[P127]
Time seemed to slow as Cheongpung’s body toppled into view.

[P128]
So did a familiar wrist—the one attached to the hand gripping the unconscious Cheongpung’s throat.

[P129]
*That’s…*

[P130]
*My hand.*

[P131]
The next thought was drowned beneath a surge of blood and pain. His mouth dropped open, and a scream tore from it.

[P132]
“Gaaaaah!”

[P133]
But it was not over.

[P134]
As the Blood Lord staggered backward, screaming, a cold voice pursued him.

[P135]
“You’ve accumulated sins that can never be washed away. Shouldn’t you pay the price?”

[P136]
Whoosh!

[P137]
Every hair on the Blood Lord’s body stood on end.

[P138]
It was like a hallucination. The entire landscape vanished, and a single sword aimed at his chest consumed his every sense.

[P139]
Shhk.

[P140]
The sword glided through the air. The violet Force of the Zaha Divine Technique transformed into thirty-six plum blossoms that scattered in every direction.

[P141]
At the beautiful sight, the Blood Lord murmured as though groaning.

[P142]
“The Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords.”

[P143]
But it was different.

[P144]
Unmistakably different.

[P145]
If the Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords Cheongpung had used earlier were a supreme technique, what Mae Jonghak now displayed was a divine feat beyond martial arts.

[P146]
And that divine feat was closing in on every vital point in the Blood Lord’s body.

[P147]
*I can’t stop this.*

[P148]
Horrified, the Blood Lord tried to throw himself aside.

[P149]
Grab!

[P150]
A hand clamped around his ankle.

[P151]
Jin Taekyung, whom he had thought spent and unconscious, grinned up at him through bloodstained teeth.

[P152]
“Where do you think you’re going, motherfucker?”

[P153]
“You—!”

[P154]
Papapapapat!

[P155]
The rest of his words never came.

[P156]
Violet flashes filled his eyes. Blood sprayed, and flesh split apart. The immense agony wiped his mind blank.

[P157]
“Ghk!”

[P158]

[P159]
Slash! Slash!

[P160]
Then, as his consciousness began to fade, the Blood Lord’s eyes suddenly flashed.

[P161]
*No. If I use that—if I use that, I can survive.*

[P162]
His mission was already complete. The Green Jade Buddha Staff in his hand—the only one left—was proof of that.

[P163]
It was regrettable that he had failed to kill the Fire King, but…

[P164]
As long as he lived, there would always be another chance.

[P165]
He glared venomously at Jin Taekyung. Taekyung was still smiling even as he coughed up clots of blood.

[P166]
“Just you wait. I’ll kill you with my own hands.”

[P167]

[P168]

[P169]
The Blood Lord’s lips curled upward.

[P170]

[P171]

[P172]

[P173]

[P174]

[P175]
Whoosh!

[P176]

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

At last, his cherished sword regained its true form and gleamed coldly.

[P121]
Hundreds—perhaps thousands. The sword that had drunk the blood of countless fiends now pointed at the Blood Lord.

[P122]
“Just as I said, isn’t this sword still useful?”

[P123]
The next instant, a violet flash erupted.

[P124]
Slash!

[P125]
“…Huh?”

[P126]
The Blood Lord blinked.

[P127]
Time seemed to slow as Cheongpung’s body toppled into view.

[P128]
So did a familiar wrist—the one attached to the hand gripping the unconscious Cheongpung’s throat.

[P129]
*That’s…*

[P130]
*My hand.*

[P131]
The next thought was drowned beneath a surge of blood and pain. His mouth dropped open, and a scream tore from it.

[P132]
“Gaaaaah!”

[P133]
But it was not over.

[P134]
As the Blood Lord staggered backward, screaming, a cold voice pursued him.

[P135]
“You’ve accumulated sins that can never be washed away. Shouldn’t you pay the price?”

[P136]
Whoosh!

[P137]
Every hair on the Blood Lord’s body stood on end.

[P138]
It was like a hallucination. The entire landscape vanished, and a single sword aimed at his chest consumed his every sense.

[P139]
Shhk.

[P140]
The sword glided through the air. The violet Force of the Zaha Divine Technique transformed into thirty-six plum blossoms that scattered in every direction.

[P141]
At the beautiful sight, the Blood Lord murmured as though groaning.

[P142]
“The Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords.”

[P143]
But it was different.

[P144]
Unmistakably different.

[P145]
If the Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords Cheongpung had used earlier were a supreme technique, what Mae Jonghak now displayed was a divine feat beyond martial arts.

[P146]
And that divine feat was closing in on every vital point in the Blood Lord’s body.

[P147]
*I can’t stop this.*

[P148]
Horrified, the Blood Lord tried to throw himself aside.

[P149]
Grab!

[P150]
A hand clamped around his ankle.

[P151]
Jin Taekyung, whom he had thought spent and unconscious, grinned up at him through bloodstained teeth.

[P152]
“Where do you think you’re going, motherfucker?”

[P153]
“You—!”

[P154]
Papapapapat!

[P155]
The rest of his words never came.

[P156]
Violet flashes filled his eyes. Blood sprayed, and flesh split apart. The immense agony wiped his mind blank.

[P157]
“Ghk!”

[P158]
This was on an entirely different level. There was no way to block the Sword Energy hurtling across more than a hundred feet.

[P159]
Slash! Slash!

[P160]
Then, as his consciousness began to fade, the Blood Lord’s eyes suddenly flashed.

[P161]
*No. If I use that—if I use that, I can survive.*

[P162]
His mission was already complete. The Green Jade Buddha Staff in his hand—the only one left—was proof of that.

[P163]
It was regrettable that he had failed to kill the Fire King, but…

[P164]
As long as he lived, there would always be another chance.

[P165]
He glared venomously at Jin Taekyung. Taekyung was still smiling even as he coughed up clots of blood.

[P166]
“Just you wait. I’ll kill you with my own hands.”

[P167]
“What?”

[P168]
“Stay alive until then. Make sure of it.”

[P169]
The Blood Lord’s lips curled upward.

[P170]
Mae Jonghak sensed something and stiffened, unleashing another burst of Sword Energy.

[P171]
“Stop!”

[P172]
Shriek! Slash!

[P173]
The Blood Lord’s one remaining arm was severed cleanly at the shoulder.

[P174]
“Lord of Heaven!”

[P175]
Whoosh!

[P176]
With that shout, he drew upon the last of his strength and shot forward like lightning. His teeth clamped down hard on his own severed arm—or rather, on the Green Jade Buddha Staff it still held.

[P177]
And then—

[P178]
Fwoom!

[P179]

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 266

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃266화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“껍질을 깼구나.”
  6|
  7|맑은 목소리가 울려 퍼졌다.
  8|
  9|청풍이 연화봉의 햇살과 푸른 하늘을 떠올린 데 비해, 혈주는 심장이 철렁 내려앉는 듯한 충격을 느꼈다.
 10|
 11|고작 이십여 장 밖의 기척을 감지하지 못했다. 다른 누구도 아닌 자신이.
 12|
 13|그는 오솔길을 걸어 올라오는 한 사람을 보며 눈매를 가늘게 떴다.
 14|
 15|‘저놈은…….’
 16|
 17|호리호리한 체구에 서글서글한 인상. 기껏해야 이십 대 중반으로 보이는 청년이다.
 18|
 19|검집도 없이 허리춤에 대충 찔러 넣은 검은 온통 붉게 녹이 슬어 있었다.
 20|
 21|혈주의 입술 사이로 메마른 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
 22|
 23|“상승검?”
 24|
 25|청년, 종리추가 빙긋 웃었다.
 26|
 27|“늘 걱정이었다.”
 28|
 29|“뭐?”
 30|
 31|“두려움을 모르는 천진난만한 아이가 무림에 나가면 얼마나 큰 파도를 겪을지.”
 32|
 33|“이게 무슨 개소리…….”
 34|
 35|말을 이으려던 혈주는 불현듯 깨달았다. 처음부터 종리추의 모든 말과 행동이 오직 한 사람에게로 향하고 있었음을.
 36|
 37|“하지만 이제 되었다. 정말 잘 이겨 내 주었어.”
 38|
 39|따스한 시선과 목소리.
 40|
 41|이윽고 힘겹게 헐떡이던 청풍의 입가에 희미한 미소가 맺혔다.
 42|
 43|그 모습을 지켜본 혈주는 헛웃음을 흘렸다.
 44|
 45|“이것들 봐라…….”
 46|
 47|이건 숫제 없는 사람 취급이 아닌가. 천(天) 내부에서도 수많은 이들의 두려움과 경외를 받는 그를 두고 말이다.
 48|
 49|하룻강아지 같은 놈들의 노골적인 무시에 저절로 손아귀에 힘이 들어갔다.
 50|
 51|우득.
 52|
 53|“커헉!”
 54|
 55|뼈 어긋나는 소리와 함께 청풍의 입술 사이로 핏물이 울컥 터져 나왔다.
 56|
 57|고통 어린 신음을 흘린 청풍이 혼절함과 동시에, 종리추의 조용한 목소리가 혈주의 귓가를 울렸다.
 58|
 59|“그만하시게.”
 60|
 61|웃음이 사라진 종리추의 얼굴을 보자 기분이 한결 나아졌다.
 62|
 63|혈주가 씩 웃으며 입을 열었다.
 64|
 65|“이제야 내가 보이는 모양이군.”
 66|
 67|“진즉에 보고 있었네. 멀어지는 뒷모습만 쫓다가 놓쳐 버렸지만.”
 68|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{
"chapter": 1,
"decisions": [
{
"hunk_id": "H001",
"decision": "SOL",
"reason": "brief specific reason"
},

},

}

}

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
